files.note: Changed between the releases: getUserByEmail's shape rule moved to TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN in src/constants.ts, with the comment that argued for it; the rule itself is unchanged. The claim now names the constant, and leaves the rationale to that file.

Changed between the releases: both user write payloads check email with TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, the lookup's shape rule, instead of z.string().email(), and UserSchema's comment now says shape check. The claim is rewritten for the shared rule; the other schemas it cites are unchanged.

Changed between the releases only in the shipped build: 9.0.0 no longer emits source maps, so dist/modules/list.js lost its trailing sourceMappingURL comment. The source is unchanged, so the claim stands.

sources.supports: Every method validates its identifier and places it as the path segment of the matching endpoint. getUserByEmail checks the address against TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, a deliberately loose shape rule, one @ with non-empty whitespace-free parts, and refuses anything else before dispatch. getUsers takes an optional project and addresses get_users/{project_id} when it is given. updateGroup injects the path identifier into the body as group_id, overwriting whatever the caller supplied, because TestRail rejects a body without it. No write payload is parsed by a public method, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

UserSchema is the reply shape and is permissive: role_id, is_admin, group_ids and the enterprise fields are all nullish because older servers omit them and get_current_user returns a reduced record, and mfa_required admits an integer because TestRail Cloud wire-encodes it as 0 or 1. UserAddPayloadSchema requires a non-empty name and an email checked with TESTRAIL_USER_EMAIL_PATTERN, the lookup's shape rule, which UserUpdatePayloadSchema applies to its optional email as well; addUser and updateUser forward the payload unparsed, so the boundary applies it. It declares role_id, group_ids and assigned_projects as positive integers; UserUpdatePayloadSchema makes every field optional. GroupSchema carries id, name and a nullish user_ids. AddGroupPayloadSchema requires name; UpdateGroupPayloadSchema makes it optional and its comment records that TestRail accepts an empty update body. RoleSchema carries id, name, is_default and a nullish is_project_admin.
listOf and unwrapList accept either a bare array or a collection wrapper, and treat a null collection as empty, so get_users resolves to an array whichever of the three shapes TestRail sends.

get_user and get_user_by_email return one user, the latter taking the address as a query parameter. get_users returns an array and accepts an optional project in the path; from TestRail 6.6 only administrators may omit it, and the project form omits inactive users, omits users holding only global access, and reports each role at its project level. add_user requires name and email and accepts is_active, is_admin, role_id, group_ids, mfa_required, email_notifications, sso_enabled and assigned_projects, with is_active defaulting to false; update_user supports the same fields. The reference's get_current_user section contradicts the endpoint's own purpose by listing a required user_id parameter while describing the user making the request.

input_policy.notes: The project is optional and is the one input in this server that sits under query while reaching the wire as a path segment: the registered route carries no placeholder because the endpoint has two forms, and supplying the project selects the second. The two forms are not one list with a filter applied, so the manifest records both.

outer_result.notes: TestRail documents a bare array here while every sibling list in the Users family documents an envelope. The driver accepts the bare array, the users wrapper and a null collection, and resolves to an array in all three cases, so a caller sees one shape whichever the server sends.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown query field rather than dropping it and widening the result.
Return the users as an array when TestRail answers with a bare array.
Return the same array when TestRail answers with a users wrapper.
Return an empty array, not an error, when TestRail answers with a null users collection.

parameters.semantics: The project to scope the list to. Omitted, the call reads every user and needs administrator access; supplied, it reads the users with explicit access to that project, which TestRail requires of non-administrators from 6.6 and which also omits inactive users, omits users holding only global access, and reports each role at its project level. The driver validates it before dispatch, so a non-positive value is the driver's refusal rather than the boundary's alone.

wire.encoding: Appended as a path segment, get_users/{project_id}; omitted entirely when the caller sends none, which is a different endpoint rather than the same one with a blank value.
